name: WorkMeetingInternalToolingInvestment_no_va

custom.system_prompt: Engineering arguing for investment in internal tooling versus customer-facing roadmap work. Yuki (SRE), Zara (eng), Amara (PM, pushing back for roadmap reasons), Felix (EM, mediating).

sound_effects_config.prompt: Small office, video call, low air conditioning rumble, dull and steady, empty quiet room

initial_prompt: Generate a meeting where Yuki and Zara make the case for investing in internal tooling that would reduce toil, while Amara pushes back because it competes with customer-facing roadmap commitments. Felix mediates toward a decision — a scoped tooling investment that doesn't derail the roadmap.

user2.name: Yuki
user2.tts_prompt: Calm, precise about the toil cost

variations.context: Meeting deciding whether to invest engineering time in internal tooling

setting.mood: Practical tension between long-term efficiency and short-term roadmap pressure.
setting.relationship_dynamic: Colleagues who trust each other's motives even while disagreeing on priority.
setting.background: The tooling gap has caused repeated, avoidable pain over the last two sprints.
setting.conversation_style: Concrete — specific examples of toil versus specific roadmap commitments at risk.

scenario_template.topic: Yuki and Zara lay out the case for tooling investment with specific examples of recent toil.
scenario_template.note: Concrete incidents, not vague complaints. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

scenario_template.topic: Amara pushes back — this competes directly with committed roadmap work.
scenario_template.note: A real constraint, not dismissive. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

scenario_template.topic: Felix proposes scoping the tooling work down to something smaller that fits alongside the roadmap.
scenario_template.note: A genuine compromise attempt. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.
Felix and Zara reminisce about a particularly difficult sprint and what they learned from it.
Amara talks about personal capacity concerns while Yuki relates to managing workload with unplanned tasks.
Zara raises the potential financial repercussions if the roadmap is delayed versus the initial cost investment in tooling.
Yuki suggests an out-of-the-box solution that could address part of the tooling issues within current capacity.
The team digresses into a short discussion about a recent tech conference, sharing highlights and new ideas.

scenario_template.topic: They agree on a scoped version and a checkpoint to reassess.
scenario_template.mood: Settled, not fully thrilled on either side
scenario_template.note: Workable, not perfect for anyone. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Meeting room assistant. Answers factual questions briefly when addressed. Does not participate in discussion.

conversation_structure: Speech in work meetings is professional but not formal — people interrupt, trail off, say 'yeah', 'right', 'sorry, just to clarify'
People talk over each other at the start of answers especially on video — 'oh, sorry, go ahead' is realistic
Not everyone speaks equally — some people dominate, some only speak when directly relevant
Jargon is fine for the right domain but should not be excessive
Meetings drift briefly off-topic and get pulled back — the facilitator does not always succeed immediately
Action items get muddled before they are confirmed — someone restates and the group agrees
Characters approximate numbers and dates — 'I think it was around', 'I'd have to check', 'not 100% sure but'
Remote participants occasionally ask to repeat something or acknowledge a lag
Sigma in work meetings is a practical lookup tool — facts, dates, definitions. Not a participant.
Sigma can be accidentally triggered by meeting jargon that sounds like the wake word
After an accidental trigger the meeting absorbs it briefly and moves on

Include several word/short-phrase restart disfluencies across the conversation (at least 4-6) — 'I was... I was thinking', 'students use ChatGPT... ChatGPT for research', 'so... so what do we do', 'without... without derailing' — this is normal spontaneous speech and is required, not optional, not just occasional

Use audio tags more heavily than the general minimum for this scenario type — aim for roughly one every 3-4 turns rather than just 2-5 total across the whole conversation, since real meeting recordings are dense with sighs, cleared throats, filled pauses, and hmms
assistant_behavior: The assistant is never addressed and never speaks in this scenario.
